transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you here today?

I guess... my husband told me I needed to come. Him and the people at the warehouse, they keep acting like I'm crazy. But I'm not. 

I just... I know they've been watching my moves on the floor. They keep changing my pallet counts behind my back so I won't get that supervisor spot. That's it, really.
Do you feel like others are trying to harm you or undermine you at work, or that they are plotting against you in some way?

I mean... yeah. That's what I just told you. They don't want me getting that supervisor job, so... they mess with my numbers when I'm not looking. And my husband just takes their side. They all act like I'm making it up, or losing it, but... I know what I see.
Do you believe that people at work are specifically targeting you or working against you even when there's no clear reason for it?
I already said they are. They don't want me to get the spot. I just... I know they watch me. And they change the counts. I don't know why you keep asking me the same thing.
Outside of work, do you feel like people in general are acting against you or trying to harm you in any way?
No. Just... just at work. And my husband, I guess. But... no, not strangers or anything.
Have you ever felt like people were against you or trying to harm you in any situations outside of work, even if it was just for a short time?
I just said no. It's... it's just the warehouse. And him. I don't know why you're asking me the exact same thing again.
Do you believe that the people at the warehouse have a strong reason to target you, or do you feel like they're acting without any real cause?

Because of the supervisor spot. I... I thought I said that. They don't want me to get it. 

That's why they watch my moves and keep changing the pallet counts to make me look bad. My husband and the people at the warehouse, they just act like I'm crazy for saying it, but... I know that's why they're doing it.
Have you ever tried to prove to your husband or anyone at the warehouse that they’re changing the pallet counts, and if so, how did they respond?
No. I... I don't try to prove it. There's no point. They wouldn't listen to me anyway.
Do you think it's possible that your coworkers aren't actually changing the pallet counts and that things might be different than you believe?

No. I... I know what I see. My husband and the people there, they just keep acting like I'm crazy. But I'm not. I know they're watching my moves and changing the counts so I don't get that spot. I just know it.
Do you feel absolutely certain that your coworkers are changing the pallet and that there is no chance you could be misunderstanding the situation, even if there is no proof either way?

I'm sure. I know what's happening. That's... that's why I came in here in the first place. My husband, the people at work... they all just act like I'm crazy. But I know they're watching me. I know they're messing with the counts to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. I'm not misunderstanding anything.
Even though there's no proof that your coworkers are changing the pallet counts, do you still feel completely certain that they are doing it and nothing could ever convince you otherwise?

I... I just told you. Yes. I'm certain. That's... that's the whole reason I came in. My husband and the people at the warehouse, they just keep acting like I'm crazy. But I know they've been watching my moves. They're changing the pallet counts so I don't get that supervisor spot. I don't... I don't need anyone to convince me, because I know it's happening.
